cluster_summary: This cluster covers vulnerabilities where user-controlled input is directly concatenated or interpolated into database query strings (SQL, JPQL, Cypher, DQL) without proper parameterization or escaping, leading to injection attacks. The majority are fixed by replacing string concatenation with parameterized queries; a subset rely on improved escaping of special characters. A few involve identifier quoting, type casting, or input validation.
guideline_text: Trace attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs into the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs. Report code paths where the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should Wrap identifiers with proper quoting (e.g., double quotes) via an escaping function..

mechanism.missing_guard: the required validation, authorization, isolation, state check, or binding is absent or not connected to the sensitive effect
mechanism.name: SQL injection via unescaped identifiers fixed by identifier quoting
mechanism.sink_shape: the sensitive operation or security boundary described by the member CVEs
mechanism.source_shape: attacker-influenced inputs, resource identities, state values, or configuration described by the member CVEs
mechanism.typical_fix: Wrap identifiers with proper quoting (e.g., double quotes) via an escaping function.

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Wrap identifiers with proper quoting (e.g., double quotes) via an escaping function.
sub_patterns.name: SQL injection via unescaped identifiers fixed by identifier quoting
sub_patterns.root_cause: User-controlled database schema names (column names, key names) are concatenated into SQL without identifier quoting, allowing an attacker to craft names that break out of the identifier context.
